Care of the Terminally Ill, Death & Dying

Terminal care — palliative care, signs of approaching death, care after death and grief support.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the goals of palliative care
  • List signs of approaching death
  • Explain care after death and grief support

In simple words

Terminal care is care for patients who are dying. The goal is comfort, dignity and relief from pain and distress — not cure. This is palliative care.

Nurses support the patient and family through dying and after death, including grief support.

Signs of approaching death

  • Decreased consciousness, more sleeping.
  • Breathing changes (Cheyne–Stokes, long pauses).
  • Cool hands and feet; mottled skin.
  • Reduced intake of food and fluids.
  • Loss of bladder and bowel control.

Care after death

  • Close the eyes; straighten the limbs.
  • Wash and dress the body; position respectfully.
  • Label the body correctly.
  • Support the family; allow time with the body.
  • Follow hospital and legal procedures (death certificate, autopsy consent).

Grief support

  • Listen; allow the family to express feelings.
  • Do not say “I know how you feel.”
  • Provide privacy and time.
  • Refer to counselling if needed.

🔴 Palliative care goal

The goal of terminal care is comfort and dignity — not cure. Relieve pain and distress; support the patient and family.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Pain and symptom control — give analgesia as prescribed; keep the patient comfortable.
  • Mouth care — keep the mouth moist; clean regularly.
  • Positioning — turn regularly; use pillows for comfort.
  • Family presence — allow the family to be with the patient; provide privacy.
  • After death — provide respectful care of the body; support the family’s grief.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Palliative care aims at comfort, dignity and relief from pain — not cure.
  2. Signs of approaching death: more sleeping, breathing changes, cool limbs, reduced intake.
  3. Care after death: close eyes, wash and dress, label body, support family.
  4. Grief support: listen, allow feelings, provide privacy, do not judge.
  5. Terminal care supports both the patient and the family.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Do not say “I know how you feel” to a grieving family.
  2. Mouth care keeps the dying patient comfortable.
  3. Follow legal procedures after death (certificate, autopsy).
  4. Refer to counselling for complicated grief.

📌 Memory trick

Care after death: “E-W-L-S” — Eyes closed, Wash, Label, Support family.

60-second revision

  • Terminal care = comfort, dignity, pain relief (palliative).
  • Signs of death: more sleeping, breathing changes, cool limbs, reduced intake.
  • After death: close eyes, wash, dress, label, support family.
  • Grief: listen, privacy, no judgement, refer if needed.
  • Goal is not cure.

Test yourself

The goal of palliative care is:

Answer: B. Palliative care focuses on comfort, dignity and symptom relief, not cure.

A sign of approaching death is:

Answer: B. Increased sleeping and decreased consciousness are common signs.

After death, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Provide respectful care — close eyes, wash, dress, label and support the family.

Grief support means:

Answer: B. Listen and allow the family to express their feelings without judgement.

Which should NOT be said to a grieving family?

Answer: B. Avoid saying ‘I know how you feel’ — everyone’s grief is unique.
